findings.reason: the case list must say which stores are expected to be skipped and exclude the pointer read and already-cached paths. Otherwise the node either writes a test that cannot pass or one whose first case proves nothing.
findings.text: the s113 case list asks that a second pass over an unchanged crew home "opens none of the run, ledger or review stores the first pass opened", and that a pass after one run's record changed opens "that run's stores and no other run's". The admit pass must re-read the live and queued pointer set every pass (`runs.list_live`, `read_pointer` in `_READ_SOURCES`, `reckon/crew/admission/service.py:220-244`); the SQLite run store is reached only through the cached plan-review authoring selection (`_stored_authoring_runs`, `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:4220-4232`, whose docstring says each row is decoded "only when it changes"), and the review store is already summarised across passes by a stat-keyed module cache (`_RECORD_SUMMARIES`, `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:1709-1778`). So the "run store" clause is vacuous where it means the SQLite store, and unachievable where it means the pointer store the pass must re-read; "that run's stores" also names a per-run scope for stores that are per project. A node implementing this literally cannot satisfy the second case as written.

findings.reason: an unverified attribution aims the node's rewrite at stores that already cache, while the 500 MB a minute gate could remain unmet by reads the section never names (readiness ledger joins, plan-file reads, pointer scans), costing a full dispatch to discover.
findings.text: the Why asserts the 68 GB a minute is "the read volume of a pass that opens the crew's whole history each time". §112's measurement records only total read volume with two worker runs live; it does not decompose the reads. In the system §113 cites, the review store is already answered from `_RECORD_SUMMARIES` keyed on each record's stat identity across passes (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:1709-1778`) and the run store's rows are decoded once per change token in the plan-review authoring path (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:4220-4232`), so "opens the crew's whole history each time" is not what the cited system shows.

findings.reason: a later reader cannot reopen the measurement that the done-when's primary numeric claim rests on, and the node has no declared place to write it.
findings.text: the headline measure is a ten-minute `/proc` read of the live admit service, but no log path is named for it and no command is pinned, unlike the arm logs it does require; only "the before and after figures are recorded in this plan's landed record" names any store.
